llm.summary: This skill is a memory-sync tool whose core purpose is disclosed, but it asks the agent to persist conversation content and run broad local or external sync actions without enough user control.

dimensions.detail: The requested behavior reaches broad local memory sources, conversation logs, Obsidian, and GitHub-oriented workflows; that access is aligned with the memory-engine purpose but high impact and under-scoped for privacy-sensitive content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package itself contains only markdown metadata and no executable implementation, but it instructs agents to run an existing local Python engine from hardcoded Windows paths that are outside the packaged artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The invocation guidance includes automatic or routine memory updates for new tasks, new conversations, daily updates, and end-of-session increments, which can capture conversation content beyond a clearly bounded user request.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly describes cross-session persistence, daily scheduled sync, incremental session writes, Obsidian export, and an 'all' mode that clears L3/L2 state before rebuilding, without requiring preview or confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is an external memory engine for vectorized retrieval, visualization, Obsidian sync, and GitHub publishing, and those capabilities are coherent with the skill description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use it only if you intentionally want an agent to write selected conversation/task content into a persistent external memory system and possibly sync it to Obsidian or GitHub. Before any use, verify the hardcoded local paths, inspect the referenced local sync.py implementation, disable or review any scheduled task, and require explicit confirmation before running all, incremental, obsidian, or any publishing workflow. Do not use it with secrets, private client data, credentials, or sensitive personal information unless you have separate retention and deletion controls.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The memory-related triggers fit the product concept, but the artifact broadens them to routine new-task, new-conversation, and daily updates, which creates real ambiguity about when persistence should occur.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documented 'all' command clears memory layers and exports to Obsidian; those operations are disclosed but high-impact, and the artifact does not include a confirmation, dry-run, or rollback requirement.
[SSD-3] expected: Cross-session persistence is central to this skill, but storing conversation and task content for later reuse remains a material privacy concern unless users explicitly scope what may be retained and synced.
